learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to mathematically model logistical issues such as material logistics, demand calculation, lot size planning, and machine scheduling.
They can analytically analyze logistical processes and planning problems and apply various mathematical methods and algorithms to solve these logistical problems.
They are capable of using discrete simulation tools for modeling and analyzing factory planning processes and interpreting the results.

syllabus_topics: Material logistics: Modeling and optimization of material flows in the factory, warehousing and inventory management
Demand calculation: Forecasting methods, deterministic and stochastic models for demand planning
Lot size planning: Models for determining optimal lot sizes, economic lot size formula, dynamic lot size planning
Machine scheduling: Scheduling problems, priority rules, machine scheduling models, capacity planning
Discrete simulation: Fundamentals of simulation technology, introduction to discrete simulation models, application and use of simulation software (e.g., AnyLogic, Plant Simulation)
Case studies and applications: Practical applications and examples to illustrate the models and methods, implementation of simulation projects in digital factory planning
teaching_methods: seminar-style instruction with active exercise component

assessment_methods.method: Combined examination (study project work and oral examination)

assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
